classification.difficultyReason: Find two nested difference areas and justify their comparison using exact expressions.

content.prompt: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius 1. The circle is then inscribed in a square, as shown below. Which is larger: the blue area or the red area?

spec.description: An axis-aligned square circumscribes a circle; an unfilled diamond-shaped square is inscribed in that circle. The two difference regions retain blue and red shading.
spec.mathematics: Circle radius 1; outer square side 2; inner square diagonal 2. All four circle tangencies coincide with the inner square vertices.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given geometric regions are shown; no areas or inferred dimensions are labelled.

answer.short:
The blue area is larger: blue $=\pi-2$, red $=4-\pi$ square units.

Their difference is $2\pi-6>0$, since $\pi>3$.
answer.worked:
The outer square has side length 2 and area 4. If the inner square has side length $s$, its diagonal is 2.

$$\begin{align*}2s^2&=2^2\\s^2&=2\\A_{\text{blue}}&=\pi(1)^2-2\\A_{\text{blue}}&=\pi-2\\A_{\text{red}}&=4-\pi(1)^2\\A_{\text{red}}&=4-\pi\\A_{\text{blue}}-A_{\text{red}}&=(\pi-2)-(4-\pi)\\A_{\text{blue}}-A_{\text{red}}&=2\pi-6.\end{align*}$$

Since $\pi>3$, this difference is positive. The blue area is larger.
